trial_court: High Court of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla Cr. MMO No. 1304 of 2022
case_name: Abhishek Bhatti And Ors vs State Of H.P. & Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: State of H.P. & Anr (wife's parents, police)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Informant married Abhishek Bhatti in 2021 but was unhappy with her husband and parents-in-law. She was turned out of her matrimonial home several times. FIR registered for offences under Sections 498A, 406, 506 IPC.

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection, and only in the rarest of rare cases.
legal_principles.held: We also give a note of caution to the effect that the power of quashing a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases;
cited_cases: Abhishek v. State of M.P., (2023) SCC OnLine SC 1083
V. Ravi Kumar v. State represented by Inspector of Police, District Crime Branch, Salem, Tamil Nadu, [(2019) 14 SCC 568]

legal_principles.principle: The court should not embark upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR or complaint when exercising its power to quash a criminal proceeding.
legal_principles.held: that the Court will not be justified in embarking upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR or the complaint and that the extraordinary or inherent powers do not confer an arbitrary jurisdiction on the court to act according to its whim or caprice.
cited_cases: V. Ravi Kumar v. State represented by Inspector of Police, District Crime Branch, Salem, Tamil Nadu, [(2019) 14 SCC 568]

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash a FIR/complaint should be exercised sparingly, with circumspection and in the rarest of rare cases.
legal_principles.held: It was observed that the power of quashing should be exercised sparingly, with circumspection and in the rarest of rare cases, such standard not being confused with the norm formulated in the context of the death penalty.
cited_cases: Neeharika Infrastructure (P). Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra [Criminal Appeal No. 330 of 2021, decided on 13.04.2021]

legal_principles.principle: The contents of the FIR and the charge sheet have to be read together to determine whether any offence is made out or not.
legal_principles.held: It was laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shaileshbhai Ranchhodbhai Patel & Anr vs State of Gujarat Criminal Appeal No.1884/2013 decided on 28.08.2024 that the contents of the FIR and the charge sheet have to be read together to determine whether any offence is made out or not.
cited_cases: Shaileshbhai Ranchhodbhai Patel & Anr vs State of Gujarat, (2024) SCC OnLine SC X

use_for_drafting: using IPC sections in DV cases
